subject: MAP: Data handling milestones & evidence for Stella Health pilot
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@stellahealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@stellahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Data handling milestones & evidence for Stella Health pilot

Thanks again for the call today — great to walk through the pilot scope. Per our conversation, attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan focused on the data handling & compliance milestones you flagged so we have shared owners and dates. High-level asks captured below; please confirm or correct and we’ll update the MAP spreadsheet.

Summary of Stella's critical constraints (as discussed)
- PHI scope: eCR/claims extracts + user-entered notes (limited to pilot clinics).
- Retention: transaction logs and audit trails must be retained for 7 years for regulated records; session-level caches can be 30 days.
- Logging: request/response audit trail with requester identity, model version, timestamp, and a redaction/obfuscation flag.
- Encryption: data-at-rest via customer KMS, TLS1.3 in transit.
- Access reviews: quarterly, with audit-ready export.

Key MAP milestones I put in the draft (owners and target dates)
1) Data Inventory & Classification — Owner: Stella (Emily) — target: 2026-11-20 — Dependency: full sample schema export
2) Retention Policy Mapping — Owner: Stella + Redwood (Karthik) — target: 2026-11-27 — Dependency: legal signoff on retention windows
3) Audit Logging Spec (fields + retention) — Owner: Redwood (Marissa) — target: 2026-12-04 — Dependency: agreed field list
4) KMS Integration plan (onboarding) — Owner: Redwood (Ben) — target: 2026-12-11 — Dependency: KMS endpoint and IAM roles
5) Evidence package delivery (SOC2 summary + sample logs) — Owner: Redwood (Olga) — target: 2026-12-18 — Dependency: completed logging spec

Immediate asks for Stella (please):
- Share minimal sample dataset/schema by EOD Fri 11/13 (can be de-identified)
- Confirm whether the 7-year retention applies to all PHI-derived artifacts or only certain classes
- Provide KMS contact and preferred key rotation cadence

Next steps from Redwood
- We’ll update the MAP spreadsheet with actionable tasks and deliverables (attached as redwood_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx).
- Marissa to draft the logging spec based on the field list you confirm.
- Ben to draft KMS integration steps and a test plan.

Attachments: redwood_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx (MAP template v1), SOC2_summary_stub.pdf (summary, stub)

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@stellahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@stellahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling milestones & evidence for Stella Health pilot

Thanks Olga — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after checking with Legal and Security: 
- The 7-year requirement applies to PHI records used for clinical decision-making and billing (transactional artifacts). We can treat ephemeral caches and derived embeddings as 1 year by default, but we need a redaction/derivation policy in the MAP.
- For audit logs, we need the following minimum fields: user_id (hashed), timestamp (UTC), action_type, model_id/version, request_id, redaction_flag, and payload_hash. The retention for logs should be configurable per-environment; for pilot prod environment we want 2 years accessible + archived for up to 7 years on cold storage.
- KMS contact: Raj Patel (cc). Our KMS runs in AWS KMS; rotation +/- quarterly.

We’ll upload a sample de-identified schema to the shared drive by 2026-11-13. Also routing this to our Privacy counsel — they may have a few redlines on retention language.

Emily
Director of Compliance | Stella Health Systems
emily.tran@stellahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0133

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling milestones & evidence for Stella Health pilot

Emily — thanks for the fast follow. Tagging updates we’ve made to the MAP and a few clarifying notes inline below. I’ll also upload a short sample audit-log snippet to the drive (sample_audit-log-snippet.txt).

Updates we applied to MAP (v1.1):
- Retention rows expanded to show separate windows for PHI records (7y), accessible logs (2y), and embeddings/derived features (1y).
- Added an action item: "Derivation & Redaction Policy" — Owner: Stella (Legal) + Redwood (Marissa) — target: 2026-11-30.
- KMS: Ben added a KMS onboarding checklist (IAM role names + network egress rules) and a test plan for envelope encryption.

Open questions for Stella (for mapping to owners in your org)
- Who in Privacy counsel should be the approver for the retention windows? Name + email please.
- For logs archived >2y, do you require immediate query capability or is cold retrieval within 48 hours acceptable?

Next actions (short):
- 11/13 — Stella: sample schema upload (Emily) — Marissa will begin logging spec draft after that.
- 11/20 — Data inventory complete (Emily) — we will run a brief intake call if there are gaps.
- 11/27 — Joint review of retention mapping (Karthik + Stella legal).
- 12/04 — Redwood provides sample logging package + verification checklist (Marissa).

If the timeline looks good I’ll mark target close date for MAP milestone set as 2026-12-18 (evidence package delivery). If you want an earlier pilot start we can compress by moving internal tasks up — Ben and I can put together a compressed test plan.

Attachments: sample_audit-log-snippet.txt

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Looping in a couple quick internal notes for readiness: 
- I started the logging spec doc; will need the sample schema and a sample event payload (Emily promised schema by 11/13). Plan to publish a first draft by 11/18 so Karthik can review retention mappings.
- Ben — I put placeholder tasks in the MAP for KMS network egress rules. Can you confirm if Redwood needs an IP allowlist or will mutual TLS suffice for your AWS KMS setup?
- Olga — I recommend we prepare two evidence bundles: (A) pilot evidence (sample logs, SOC2 summary) for Stella's internal reviewers, and (B) a hardened package for procurement/legal that includes our KMS onboarding checklist and redaction policy draft.

I’ll attach my logging spec stub to the MAP folder once the schema lands.

-Marissa
